header: House prep recipes from Australian native ingredients (after
20261018040000). Stage 4G of the bottle catalog plan:
* Four house preps get a recipe from the pages they cite, Australian
producers' own recipes first (three are new catalog rows; Macadamia
orgeat existed and moves from Syrup to Orgeat): lemon myrtle syrup (Warndu),
wattleseed syrup (Outback Spirit), macadamia orgeat (the Australian
Macadamia Society, two sources) and anise myrtle syrup (Warndu). FSANZ
lists lemon myrtle and wattleseed as traditional, not novel, foods.
* Strawberry gum waits for a toxicity check (it's a eucalyptus, and
FSANZ has no record of it as a food); other natives had no published
* One new plain ingredient: Anise myrtle.
* An independent second check of every fact in this stage (16) against
the cited pages found none wrong.

ingredients.name: Anise myrtle
ingredients.description: Dried, milled leaf of an Australian rainforest tree (Syzygium anisatum) with a sweet aniseed and liquorice flavour. Used in teas, syrups and baking.

preps.name: Anise myrtle syrup
preps.description: A sugar syrup made on an overnight anise myrtle tea, with a soft aniseed and liquorice flavour. For sours, highballs and anywhere a gentle anise note suits.

steps.body: Pour the boiling water over the anise myrtle in a heatproof bowl, cover with a cloth and leave overnight at room temperature.
Strain into a saucepan, pressing the leaf to get all the liquid out.
Add the sugar and warm gently, stirring, until it has dissolved. Do not let it boil.
Cool, bottle and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: Warndu (native food producer) anise myrtle granita: 4 tsp anise myrtle steeped overnight in 480 ml boiling water, strained, then 500 g caster sugar dissolved without boiling. We stop at that syrup stage, before freezing. Used as given.

preps.name: Lemon myrtle syrup
preps.description: Raw sugar ground with dried lemon myrtle leaf and a little finger lime, then dissolved in an equal volume of water. A bright, lemongrass-scented syrup for gin sours, Collinses and native-botanical highballs.

recipe.note: dried finger lime chips; up to double for more tang

steps.body: Grind the raw sugar, dried lemon myrtle leaves and finger lime chips together in a spice grinder until fine.
Put the flavoured sugar and the water in a small pan over medium heat and simmer only until the sugar has dissolved.
Let it cool, bottle it and keep it in the fridge.

sources.note: Warndu (native food producer): 3 tbsp raw sugar ground with 8 to 10 dried lemon myrtle leaves and 1 to 2 tsp finger lime chips, simmered with 3 tbsp water. Taken as 37.5 g sugar (1 tbsp 12.5 g), 9 leaves, 1 tsp chips, 45 ml water; scaled x8. The method's 'lemon balm' is the page's slip for its lemon myrtle sugar.

preps.name: Macadamia orgeat
preps.description: An orgeat made with ground macadamias in place of almonds, steeped overnight in a hot sugar syrup with a little orange flower water. Rich and buttery, for tiki drinks, sours and long drinks with soda.

steps.body: Pulse the macadamias in a food processor until finely ground.
Bring the sugar and water to the boil, stirring to dissolve, then simmer for 3 to 4 minutes to reduce slightly.
Stir in the ground macadamias and bring back to the boil.
Take off the heat, add the orange flower water, cover and leave to stand for about 8 hours or overnight.
Strain through a fine strainer, pressing the nuts, then bottle and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: Australian Macadamia Society (the growers' body): 2 cups macadamias, 1.5 cups raw caster sugar, 1.25 cups water, 0.5 tsp orange flower water, steeped about 8 h. Converted (nuts 134 g a cup per USDA FoodData Central 170178, sugar 200 g a cup, 240 ml a cup) and doubled.

Jono Carr (Door Knock, Sydney): 250 g macadamias simmered in 1 L almond milk, blended with 200 ml bought orgeat, 15 ml each orange blossom and rose water, salt. Much less sweet and built on almond milk; we use the Australian Macadamia Society ratio.

preps.name: Wattleseed syrup
preps.description: Caster and brown sugar simmered with roasted ground wattleseed and reduced by a third, for a rich syrup with a nutty, coffee-like flavour. Made for whisky and brandy drinks such as an Athol Brose, Espresso Martini riffs and desserts.

keeps.storage: Sterile bottle sealed hot; fridge once open

steps.body: Warm the water with the caster and brown sugar in a heavy pan until the sugar has dissolved.
Add the ground wattleseed, bring to the boil, then lower the heat and simmer gently until the volume is down by a third.
Strain through muslin for a clear syrup, twice if needed (or leave the grounds in if you don't mind the specks).
Pour hot into sterilised bottles and seal. The producer says sealed jars keep up to a year; once opened, keep it in the fridge.

sources.note: Outback Spirit (native food producer): 1 cup caster sugar, 3/4 cup brown sugar, 1 cup water, 1 tbsp (20 g) roasted ground wattleseed, reduced by a third. Converted at 1 cup sugar 200 g, 1 cup water 240 ml; batch as written.
The page states the batch makes 2 cups (500 ml).
